evals.expected_output: A customization block that adds consistent autoLayout, preserves the existing drill-down, and uses at most a minimal rank hint for an obvious anchor such as the user.
expectations: Because the user explicitly asked for left-to-right reading, the response may add `autoLayout LeftRight`.
If the response uses `rank`, it keeps it sparse and focuses on an obvious anchor such as the user rather than ranking most elements.
The response avoids gratuitous `rank same` or a pile of source/sink directives that would make the view brittle.
The response preserves or adds a stable `navigateTo` on the web application element without inventing a new structural design.
The response stays within customization scope and introduces neither hex color codes nor unnecessary structural rework.

evals.expected_output: A `style`-based customization using shared palette names (`primary`, `muted`, etc.) that highlights API elements while keeping context visible.
expectations: The response uses shared palette names (`primary`, `muted`, etc.) instead of hex codes.
The response uses `style` rules or `with` blocks to highlight API elements and de-emphasize the rest.
The response preserves structural context instead of hiding it completely.

evals.expected_output: A customization block with `link https://... '...'`, a stable `navigateTo` to the existing detail view, and no scope drift beyond this skill.
expectations: The response adds an explicit `link https://... '...'`.
The response keeps or adds a stable `navigateTo` on the web application element.
The response targets an existing detail view and stays in customization scope without rebuilding the whole view.

evals.expected_output: The response combines style, `navigateTo`, and `link` within one customization scope, then delegates structural changes to the right skill.
expectations: The response uses view customization (`style`, `navigateTo`, `link`) and the shared palette, without rebuilding the entire view.
The response keeps or adds a stable `navigateTo` for the web application detail view.
The response adds an explicit `link https://... '...'` compatible with the rest of the block.
The response delegates creation of a new structural or C3 view to `design-view`, not this skill.

evals.expected_output: A light-touch customization centered on `autoLayout` and, at most, one obvious `rank source`, with explicit restraint about adding more rank hints.
expectations: The response prefers `autoLayout` as the primary layout control.
The response does not force `autoLayout LeftRight` when the user did not ask for that reading direction.
If the response adds `rank`, it limits it to one obvious anchor such as the user as `rank source`.
The response explicitly avoids or warns against stacking multiple `rank same`/`rank source`/`rank sink` directives.
The response stays within customization scope and does not redesign the view structure.
